label: BEGINS_1: the time before every populated moment of a history has a first moment
term: contingent concrete reality begins (first moment of the time before populated moments)
definition: BEGINS_1. FirstMomentBeginningAt h Concrete v holds when some contingent concrete individual is present at some moment of history v, and the time before every moment at which one is present has a first moment (BegunComingToBe.BegunAt: some moment at or before it has no earlier moment). It constrains time, not contingent reality: it does not say when contingent reality began. Examples: discrete time with a first moment; continuous time with a first moment, such as the non-negative reals. Non-examples: an endless succession of populated days; a populated past that is open below and of finite duration, as in standard FLRW cosmology, whose initial singularity is not a moment; integer time that is empty before 0 and populated from 0 on, in which contingent reality began at 0 but time has no first moment. Over-inclusion: non-negative real time empty at 0 and populated after it satisfies BEGINS_1 although there is no first populated moment. The first moment need not be populated; nothing is said about what is present at it or about a cause.
note: Analyst order-theoretic sense; attribution deferred. It is the order notion of the A3 prime w premise (BegunAt), applied to every populated moment of one history. It is distinct from BEGINS_2 (finite duration, which an open-below past satisfies), from the schematic Scenario predicate BEGINS_3, and from the unformalized sense of a first populated moment after emptiness (related to A3). In linear time it gives BEGINS_2 for every real clock (possiblyFiniteDurationOfFirstMoment); the converse fails (MetricBeginningArrival control 2).
